title: Shadowing: stepwise rollout plan & safety notes
content:
Purpose
- Capture a minimal, pragmatic stepwise plan for introducing a new model variant behind shadowing (non-impacting) and then progressively soft-cutting traffic, with explicit safety gates and quick rollback/kill paths.

High-level goals (what success looks like)
- No customer-facing error-rate changes > 0.1% absolute.
- Latency 95p within +20% of baseline for the vast majority of requests.
- Evidence that qualitative output regressions are limited (hand-sampled diffing across 3 prompt sets).
- Warm caches primed for stable token cost before any live traffic flip.

Quick glossary
- shadowing: duplicate live requests to new variant; responses are discarded for production routing, recorded for analysis.
- soft-cut: start routing a tiny fraction of live traffic with fast circuit-breakers.
- handshake: client-level opt-in window to allow stateful priming without exposing users to regressions.

Stepwise plan
1) Preflight (dev-only, 1–2 days)
   - run unit + integration tests against the new model container.
   - perf smoke: generate 1k synthetic requests that match typical seq len distribution. Verify memory, GPU usage, and KV cache behavior.
   - set up a new metrics exporter prefix: metric namespace rwn/new-variant/

2) Shadowing (48–72 hours)
   - start at 5% sampled duplicate of live traffic (probabilistic sampling across tenants).
   - record: token counts, latency histogram, model errors/exceptions, model-version id, output checksum, top-k logits summary.
   - run nightly diff job: compare outputs to baseline for 3 prompt suites (billing prompts, safety prompts, SLO-critical prompts). Produce daily summary (pass/fail thresholds).
   - waveform alarm: if shadow-err-rate > baseline + 0.2% OR shadow-95p latency > baseline-95p + 30% for > 15 min => auto-pause further progression and page on-call.

3) Warm priming & cache bake (24–36 hours overlap with shadowing)
   - select warm cohorts (internal tenants) and send synthetic sequences to build KV caches (no user-visible changes).
   - record cache hit ratio, per-tenant latency change.
   - ensure cold-start tail latency fixed within acceptable bound.

4) Canary (soft-cut) phase 0: micro cohorts (6–12 hours)
   - route 0.05% real traffic split across geographically diverse clients with client handshake toggles enabled.
   - monitor: errors, latency, cost per token, user-side errors (4xx/5xx), semantic regression quick-check (automated heuristics).
   - manual check: product owner sign-off after 3 successful hours.

5) Canary phase 1: expanded cohorts (24–48 hours)
   - ramp to 0.5% traffic with circuit-breaker thresholds: error-rate delta +0.15% OR p95 delta +25% triggers instant rollback for affected cohort.
   - continue daily qualitative sampling and run a-b reranking eval on a small production trace.

6) Canary phase 2: broad soft-cut (48–72 hours)
   - ramp to 5% in tapered steps (0.5 -> 1.5 -> 3 -> 5) with 2x observation windows at each step.
   - posture: enable auto-fallback to baseline model for specific tenants if degradation observed.

7) Post-rollout regression watch (7 days)
   - maintain shadowing and a reduced ramp at 5% for full week to catch slow drift.
   - run scheduled quality evals and: precision/recall checks for reranking, hallucination heuristics on dialogue logs, user complaint channel watch.

Instrumentation / dashboards to prep before starting
- Per-tenant error-rate (baseline vs variant), p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost delta, total tokens consumed.
- Output-diff heatmap: fraction of responses with top-1 token mismatch > threshold per prompt set.
- Quick-scan UI for sampled pairs (baseline vs variant) with red/yellow/green triage buttons.
- Rollback control: single-click kill that reverts routing slices and unpins variant from deployer.

Safety gates & thresholds (proposal)
- Immediate abort if overall error-rate delta > 0.3% absolute for > 5 minutes.
- Immediate abort if p99 increases > 50% sustained for 10 minutes.
- Soft hold if quality regression metric (automated score) degrades > 5% for 2 successive runs.
- Manual approval required to exceed 5% traffic in any region.

Operational playbook (cheat sheet)
- On-call paging: what to say: "New-variant ramping: observed spike in p95 for tenant X at T+2m. Reverting routing slice. Investigating model cache pressure."
- Quick rollback steps:
   1) open release console -> routing -> select variant slice -> revert to baseline (toggle).
   2) if console unresponsive: run CLI command: rwinfctl route revert --slice <id> --reason "p95 spike".
   3) re-evaluate shadow logs for root cause.
- If rollback fails or traffic continues hitting variant cluster: disable cluster at infra layer (k8s scale down) and notify infra on-call.

Data collection checklist
- store shadowed request/response pairs for 7 days (PID hashed).
- keep per-tenant telemetry for 14 days.
- export sample set to secure S3 for offline evals (path: s3://redwood-evals/new-variant/).

Unresolved questions / TODOs
- Threshold values above are conservative guesses; validate with infra SRE (Leah) on what latency deltas are realistic for model X.
- Decide retention policy for full response texts vs checksums for privacy-sensitive tenants.
- Add postmortem template for any regression discovered during shadowing.
- Confirm CLI revert command exists in current release (PR 1782 references a few missing flags).

Notes to self (short-term tasks)
- Wire up the heatmap UI: reach out to Marco for a quick prototype (2 days).
- Add nightly diff job to cron: team infra ticket ENG-3421.
- Run a simulated rollback drill this week during quiet window (Wed 02:00–03:00 PST).

Very small risk mitigations (cheap wins)
- Prioritize routing by tenant weight: always pick low-volume tenants for early phases.
- Enable verbose model-side logging only for sampled requests to avoid noise/cost.
- Use a separate metric prefix to avoid accidental alert noise merging with baseline.

Post-rollout retrospective agenda (30–40m)
- What worked (10m)
- What surprised us (10m)
- Data gaps + follow-ups (10m)

If anything looks off while I'm out: follow rollback cheat sheet, keep shadowing on until I ack, and ping me on Slack (ryan.p).

-- end --
